learningObjectives: Select and justify case locking in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

elements.description: Allow one user applies an exclusive lock when opening a case for editing. Allow multiple users permits concurrent opening and checks whether the persisted case changed when saving; a stale user must refresh. Locking protects data consistency and is separate from authorization.

elements.text: Worked example: Two coordinators open a booking. With multiple-user locking, the first saves a new date; the second must refresh and reconcile rather than overwrite that update. Use one-user locking when a long edit must be exclusive.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Concurrent access is not last-writer-wins
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Allow multiple users means blindly overwrite on save.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Detect intervening changes and require refresh.

examPitfalls.title: Lock versus permission
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A lock grants a user access to confidential data.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A claims calculation requires exclusive editing while an adjuster prepares it. Which case locking strategy fits?

options.text: Disable authorization
Use a field-value list
Allow one user
Allow multiple users without conflict checks

practiceQuiz.rationale: An exclusive edit lock prevents another editor from changing the case during that edit. Field values and authorization do not implement concurrency control.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two agents open the same case under Allow multiple users. Agent A saves first. What should Agent B do if the saved case has changed?

options.text: Disable the SLA
Refresh and reconcile before saving
Force an unconditional overwrite
Delete Agent A's assignment

practiceQuiz.rationale: Optimistic concurrency detects stale data at save. Refreshing preserves the prior save and lets the user apply changes to current data.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements describe Allow multiple users?

options.text: Several users may open the case
The system checks for an intervening change before saving
All writes bypass conflict detection
Every editor receives a separate independent case automatically

practiceQuiz.rationale: Concurrent opening and save-time conflict detection are the defining behavior. The users still share one case instance.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A second operator sees that a case is locked. Does waiting for the lock establish permission to read sensitive fields?

options.text: Yes; every unlocked case is public
Yes; urgency grants field access
Only if the operator has the same timezone
No; authorization must still permit access

practiceQuiz.rationale: Locks coordinate writers. Access rules and policies determine what the operator may access.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which failure does case locking primarily prevent?

options.text: Incorrect translations
A missing ruleset prerequisite
Conflicting updates overwriting each other's data
Every connector timeout

practiceQuiz.rationale: The locking strategy addresses concurrent changes to shared case data, not integration availability or ruleset setup.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An exclusive edit lock has expired while another operator saved. Which assumption is unsafe?

options.text: The users may need to reconcile overlapping changes
The first editor can save its old snapshot without checking
The first editor should reload current data
The edit needs a valid lock when committing

practiceQuiz.rationale: An expired lock does not reserve ownership forever. Saving stale state can overwrite another operator's work.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A case type has parallel review tasks. Which requirement favors multiple-user locking?

options.text: Reviewers need concurrent access, with save conflicts handled
Every field is confidential
A single editor must hold exclusive access for the whole task
The application has only one ruleset

practiceQuiz.rationale: Concurrent work is supported when the design accepts refresh/reconciliation. Confidentiality is a separate access-control concern.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which test most directly validates a concurrency design?

options.text: Run a quiz about case terminology
Change only the portal theme
Export a ruleset without opening a case
Open the same case in two sessions, save changes and observe the second save

practiceQuiz.rationale: A two-session stale-save test exercises the actual lock and conflict behavior rather than only configuration metadata.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
